1: # Authorization
2: **Warning:** **Ads Management Standard Access is now Marketing API Access Tier**
3: **No code changes are needed.**
4: Tier labels have been updated: "Standard Access" is now **Limited Access**, and "Advanced Access" is now **Full Access**. The revised qualification threshold for Full Access has been reduced from 1,500 to **500 Marketing API calls** in the past 15 days. The underlying permission identifier remains the same, and existing access levels are preserved automatically. Learn more in the [Marketing API Access Tier documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/features-reference#marketing-api-access-tier).
5: The authorization process verifies the users and apps that will be accessing the Marketing API and grants them permissions.
6: ## App Roles
7: In your app's dashboard, you can set roles for yourself or team members as necessary: Admin, Developer, Tester.
8: **Note:** Depending on your intended use case, you may need to submit your app for review to gain access to specific permissions related to ad management.
9: ## Access Levels, Permissions, and Features
10: Business apps are subject to an additional layer of Graph API authorization called [access levels](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/overview/access-levels). During [App Review](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/app-review), your app must also request specific permissions and features.
11: **Warning:** All developers must follow all Meta [Platform Terms](https://developers.facebook.com/terms) and [Developer Policies](https://developers.facebook.com/devpolicy). **Calls on ANY access level are against production data.**
12: ### Marketing API Access Levels vs. Marketing API Access Tier
13: Permissions and features for apps have two different access levels: standard access and advanced access (**Note:** The use of the term "standard access" here refers to platform-wide access levels and is not related to the [Marketing API Access Tier](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/features-reference#marketing-api-access-tier), which has its own tiers: "Limited access" and "Full access".) To upgrade your Marketing API Access Tier, your app must meet the requirements shown in the App Dashboard.
14: #### Marketing API Access Tier overview
15: The Marketing API Access Tier controls your rate limits, Business Manager access, and system user capacity. Your tier is determined by whether your app has been approved through App Review.
16: | | Limited access (default) | Full access (after App Review) |
17: | --- | --- | --- |
18: | **How to get** | Automatically granted when you add the Marketing API product to your app. | Click **+Upgrade** for the Marketing API Access Tier feature in your App Dashboard. Your app must meet the [requirements below](#get-full-access). |
19: | **Rate limits** | Heavily rate-limited per ad account. For development only. Not for production apps running for live advertisers. | Lightly [rate limited](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/marketing-api/overview/rate-limiting) per ad account. |
20: | **Account limits** | Manage an unlimited number of ad accounts. App admins or developers can make API calls on behalf of ad account admins or advertisers. | Manage an unlimited number of ad accounts, assuming you get `ads_read` or `ads_management` permission from the ad account. |
21: | **Business Manager** | Limited access to [Business Manager](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/business-manager-api) and [Catalog](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/catalog) APIs. No Business Manager access to manage ad accounts, user permissions, and Pages. | Access to all [Business Manager](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/business-manager-api) and [Catalog](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/catalog) APIs. |
22: | **System users** | Can create 1 [system user](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/system-users) and 1 admin system user. | Can create 10 [system users](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/system-users) and 1 admin system user. |
23: | **Page creation** | Cannot create Pages through the API. | Cannot create Pages through the API. |
24: To check your current access level, go to **App Dashboard** > **App Review** > **Permissions and Features**.
25: ### Permissions and Features
26: #### Permissions
27: The permissions you should request change depending on which API you want to access.
28: If your app is only managing your ad account, standard access to the `ads_read` and `ads_management` permissions are sufficient. If your app is managing other people's ad accounts, you need advanced access to the `ads_read` and/or `ads_management` permissions. See all [available permissions for business apps](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/development/create-an-app/app-dashboard/app-types#available-permissions-2).
29: #### Features
30: The features you should request change depending on how you want to use our APIs. If you're managing ads, a common feature to request is Marketing API Access Tier. See [all available features for business apps](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/development/create-an-app/app-dashboard/app-types#available-features-2).
31: ##### Feature access levels
32: | Feature Access Level | Description |
33: | --- | --- |
34: | [Standard access](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/overview/access-levels#standard-access) | Business apps are automatically approved for standard access for all permissions and features available to the Business app type.<br><br>Use this option if you're getting started. You can build end-to-end workflows before requesting full permissions, and you can access an unlimited number of ad accounts.<br><br>Some API calls may not be available with standard access because they may belong to multiple accounts or the affected account can't be identified programmatically. |
35: | [Advanced access](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/overview/access-levels#advanced-access) | Advanced access must be approved through the [App Review](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/app-review) process on an individual permission and feature basis.<br><br>1. To request advanced access, go to your app's dashboard and click **App Review** > **Permissions and Features**.<br>2. Find the permission or feature you would like to access and, under **Action**, click **Request advanced access**. You can select one or more features. Once you have selected your options, click **Continue the Request**. You'll be taken to a screen that guides you through the submission process.<br><br>After you submit your information, Meta responds with an approval or denial and additional information if your app is not qualified for standard access.<br><br>If you're approved for advanced access, you need to do the following to maintain your status:<br><br>* Have successfully made at least 500 Marketing API calls in the last 15 days.<br>* Have made Marketing API calls with an error rate of less than 15% in the last 500 calls.<br><br>**Note:** These requirements also apply to upgrading your Marketing API Access Tier from Limited access to Full access. See [Get Full access](#get-full-access) for details. |
36: ##### Get Full access
37: In order to get Full access of Marketing API Access Tier, your app needs to meet these requirements:
38: * Have successfully made at least 500 Marketing API calls in the last 15 days.
39: * Have made Marketing API calls with an error rate of less than 15% in the last 500 calls.
40: If you're managing someone's ads, use the `scope` parameter to prompt them for the `ads_management` or `ads_read` permissions. Your app gets access when they click **Allow**.
41: ```html
42: https://www.facebook.com/v27.0/dialog/oauth?
43: client_id=<YOUR_APP_ID>
44: &redirect_uri=<YOUR_URL>
45: &scope=ads_management
46: ```
47: **Note:** When inputting the `YOUR_URL` field, put a trailing `/` (for example, http://www.facebook.com/).
48: ##### Example Use Cases
49: | Use Case | What To Request |
50: | --- | --- |
51: | You want to read and manage ads for ad accounts you own or have been granted access to by the ad account owner. | * **Permission:** `ads_management`<br>* **Feature:** Marketing API Access Tier |
52: | You want to read ad reports for ad accounts you own or have been granted access to by the ad account owner. | * **Permission:** `ads_read`<br>* **Feature:** Marketing API Access Tier |
53: | You want to pull ad reports from a set of clients and to both read and manage ads from another set of clients. | * **Permissions:** `ads_management` and `ads_read`<br>* **Feature:** Marketing API Access Tier |
54: ## Business Verification
55: Business verification is a process that allows us to verify your identity as a business entity, which we require if your app will access sensitive data. Learn more about the [Business Verification](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/apps/business-verification) process.
56: ## Learn More
57: - [Permissions Reference for Meta Technologies APIs](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/permissions)
58: ---

1: # Authorization
2: **Warning:** **Ads Management Standard Access is now Marketing API Access Tier**
3: **No code changes are needed.**
4: Tier labels have been updated: "Standard Access" is now **Limited Access**, and "Advanced Access" is now **Full Access**. The revised qualification threshold for Full Access has been reduced from 1,500 to **500 Marketing API calls** in the past 15 days. The underlying permission identifier remains the same, and existing access levels are preserved automatically. Learn more in the [Marketing API Access Tier documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/features-reference#marketing-api-access-tier).
5: The authorization process verifies the users and apps that will be accessing the Marketing API and grants them permissions.
6: ## App Roles
7: In your app's dashboard, you can set roles for yourself or team members as necessary: Admin, Developer, Tester.
8: **Note:** Depending on your intended use case, you may need to submit your app for review to gain access to specific permissions related to ad management.
9: ## Access Levels, Permissions, and Features
10: Business apps are subject to an additional layer of Graph API authorization called [access levels](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/overview/access-levels). During [App Review](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/app-review), your app must also request specific permissions and features.
11: **Warning:** All developers must follow all Meta [Platform Terms](https://developers.facebook.com/terms) and [Developer Policies](https://developers.facebook.com/devpolicy). **Calls on ANY access level are against production data.**
12: ### Marketing API Access Levels vs. Marketing API Access Tier
13: Permissions and features for apps have two different access levels: standard access and advanced access (**Note:** The use of the term "standard access" here refers to platform-wide access levels and is not related to the [Marketing API Access Tier](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/features-reference#marketing-api-access-tier), which has its own tiers: "Limited access" and "Full access".) To upgrade your Marketing API Access Tier, your app must meet the requirements shown in the App Dashboard.
14: #### Marketing API Access Tier overview
15: The Marketing API Access Tier controls your rate limits, Business Manager access, and system user capacity. Your tier is determined by whether your app has been approved through App Review.
16: | | Limited access (default) | Full access (after App Review) |
17: | --- | --- | --- |
18: | **How to get** | Automatically granted when you add the Marketing API product to your app. | Click **+Upgrade** for the Marketing API Access Tier feature in your App Dashboard. Your app must meet the [requirements below](#get-full-access). |
19: | **Rate limits** | Heavily rate-limited per ad account. For development only. Not for production apps running for live advertisers. | Lightly [rate limited](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/marketing-api/overview/rate-limiting) per ad account. |
20: | **Account limits** | Manage an unlimited number of ad accounts. App admins or developers can make API calls on behalf of ad account admins or advertisers. | Manage an unlimited number of ad accounts, assuming you get `ads_read` or `ads_management` permission from the ad account. |
21: | **Business Manager** | Limited access to [Business Manager](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/business-manager-api) and [Catalog](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/catalog) APIs. No Business Manager access to manage ad accounts, user permissions, and Pages. | Access to all [Business Manager](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/business-manager-api) and [Catalog](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/catalog) APIs. |
22: | **System users** | Can create 1 [system user](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/system-users) and 1 admin system user. | Can create 10 [system users](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/system-users) and 1 admin system user. |
23: | **Page creation** | Cannot create Pages through the API. | Cannot create Pages through the API. |
24: To check your current access level, go to **App Dashboard** > **App Review** > **Permissions and Features**.
25: ### Permissions and Features
26: #### Permissions
27: The permissions you should request change depending on which API you want to access.
28: If your app is only managing your ad account, standard access to the `ads_read` and `ads_management` permissions are sufficient. If your app is managing other people's ad accounts, you need advanced access to the `ads_read` and/or `ads_management` permissions. See all [available permissions for business apps](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/development/create-an-app/app-dashboard/app-types#available-permissions-2).
29: #### Features
30: The features you should request change depending on how you want to use our APIs. If you're managing ads, a common feature to request is Marketing API Access Tier. See [all available features for business apps](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/development/create-an-app/app-dashboard/app-types#available-features-2).
31: ##### Feature access levels
32: | Feature Access Level | Description |
33: | --- | --- |
34: | [Standard access](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/overview/access-levels#standard-access) | Business apps are automatically approved for standard access for all permissions and features available to the Business app type.<br><br>Use this option if you're getting started. You can build end-to-end workflows before requesting full permissions, and you can access an unlimited number of ad accounts.<br><br>Some API calls may not be available with standard access because they may belong to multiple accounts or the affected account can't be identified programmatically. |
35: | [Advanced access](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/graph-api/overview/access-levels#advanced-access) | Advanced access must be approved through the [App Review](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/app-review) process on an individual permission and feature basis.<br><br>1. To request advanced access, go to your app's dashboard and click **App Review** > **Permissions and Features**.<br>2. Find the permission or feature you would like to access and, under **Action**, click **Request advanced access**. You can select one or more features. Once you have selected your options, click **Continue the Request**. You'll be taken to a screen that guides you through the submission process.<br><br>After you submit your information, Meta responds with an approval or denial and additional information if your app is not qualified for standard access.<br><br>If you're approved for advanced access, you need to do the following to maintain your status:<br><br>* Have successfully made at least 500 Marketing API calls in the last 15 days.<br>* Have made Marketing API calls with an error rate of less than 15% in the last 500 calls.<br><br>**Note:** These requirements also apply to upgrading your Marketing API Access Tier from Limited access to Full access. See [Get Full access](#get-full-access) for details. |
36: ##### Get Full access
37: In order to get Full access of Marketing API Access Tier, your app needs to meet these requirements:
38: * Have successfully made at least 500 Marketing API calls in the last 15 days.
39: * Have made Marketing API calls with an error rate of less than 15% in the last 500 calls.
40: If you're managing someone's ads, use the `scope` parameter to prompt them for the `ads_management` or `ads_read` permissions. Your app gets access when they click **Allow**.
41: ```html
42: https://www.facebook.com/v27.0/dialog/oauth?
43: client_id=<YOUR_APP_ID>
44: &redirect_uri=<YOUR_URL>
45: &scope=ads_management
46: ```
47: **Note:** When inputting the `YOUR_URL` field, put a trailing `/` (for example, http://www.facebook.com/).
48: ##### Example Use Cases
49: | Use Case | What To Request |
50: | --- | --- |
51: | You want to read and manage ads for ad accounts you own or have been granted access to by the ad account owner. | * **Permission:** `ads_management`<br>* **Feature:** Marketing API Access Tier |
52: | You want to read ad reports for ad accounts you own or have been granted access to by the ad account owner. | * **Permission:** `ads_read`<br>* **Feature:** Marketing API Access Tier |
53: | You want to pull ad reports from a set of clients and to both read and manage ads from another set of clients. | * **Permissions:** `ads_management` and `ads_read`<br>* **Feature:** Marketing API Access Tier |
54: ## Business Verification
55: Business verification is a process that allows us to verify your identity as a business entity, which we require if your app will access sensitive data. Learn more about the [Business Verification](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/apps/business-verification) process.
56: ## Learn More
57: - [Permissions Reference for Meta Technologies APIs](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/permissions)
58: ---

sources.numbered_text: 1: # Facebook Business SDK for Python 2: [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/facebook-business)](https://pypi.org/project/facebook-business/) 3: [![Build Status](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/facebook/facebook-python-business-sdk/ci.yml)](https://github.com/facebook/facebook-python-business-sdk/actions/workflows/ci.yml) 4: [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Facebook%20Platform-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/facebook/facebook-python-business-sdk/blob/main/LICENSE.txt) 5: ### Introduction 6: The Facebook Business SDK is a one-stop-shop to help our partners better serve their businesses. Partners are using multiple Facebook API's to serve the needs of their clients. Adopting all these API's and keeping them up to date across the various platforms can be time consuming and ultimately prohibitive. For this reason Facebook has developed the Business SDK bundling many of its APIs into one SDK to ease implementation and upkeep. The Business SDK is an upgraded version of the Marketing API SDK that includes the Marketing API as well as many Facebook APIs from different platforms such as Pages, Business Manager, Instagram, etc. 7: ## Quick Start 8: Business SDK Getting Started Guide 9: Python is currently the most popular language for our third-party developers. `facebook_business` is a Python package that provides an interface between your Python application and Facebook's APIs within the Business SDK. This tutorial covers the basic knowledge needed to use the SDK and provides some exercises for the reader. 10: **NOTE**: ``facebook_business`` package is compatible with Python 2 and 3! 11: ## Pre-requisites 12: ### Register An App 13: To get started with the SDK, you must have an app 14: registered on developers.facebook.com. 15: To manage the Marketing API, please visit your 16: App Dashboard 17: and add the Marketing API product to your app. 18: **IMPORTANT**: For security, it is recommended that you turn on 'App Secret 19: Proof for Server API calls' in your app's Settings->Advanced page. 20: ### Obtain An Access Token 21: When someone connects with an app using Facebook Login and approves the request 22: for permissions, the app obtains an access token that provides temporary, secure 23: access to Facebook APIs. 24: An access token is an opaque string that identifies a User, app, or Page. 25: For example, to access the Marketing API, you need to generate a user access token 26: for your app and ask for the ``ads_management`` permission; to access Pages API, 27: you need to generate a Page access token for your app and ask for the ``manage_page`` permission. 28: Refer to our 29: 30: Access Token Guide to learn more. 31: For now, we can use the 32: Graph Explorer 33: to get an access token. 34: ## Install package 35: The easiest way to install the SDK is via ``pip`` in your shell. 36: **NOTE**: For Python 3, use ``pip3`` and ``python3`` instead. 37: **NOTE**: Use ``sudo`` if any of these complain about permissions. (This might 38: happen if you are using a system installed Python.) 39: If you don't have pip: 40: ``` 41: easy_install pip 42: ``` 43: Now execute when you have pip: 44: ``` 45: pip install facebook_business 46: ``` 47: If you care for the latest version instead of a possibly outdated version in the 48: pypi.python.org repository, 49: check out the 50: repository from GitHub or download a release tarball. Once you've got the 51: package downloaded and unzipped, install it: 52: ``` 53: python setup.py install 54: ``` 55: Great, now you are ready to use the SDK! 56: ## Bootstrapping 57: ### Create test.py 58: Create a test.py file with the contents below (assuming your system is using python 2.7 and installed under /opt/homebrew. Update to your proper python location.): 59: ```python 60: import sys 61: sys.path.append('/opt/homebrew/lib/python2.7/site-packages') # Replace this with the place you installed facebookads using pip 62: sys.path.append('/opt/homebrew/lib/python2.7/site-packages/facebook_business-3.0.0-py2.7.egg-info') # same as above 63: from facebook_business.api import FacebookAdsApi 64: from facebook_business.adobjects.adaccount import AdAccount 65: my_app_id = 'your-app-id' 66: my_app_secret = 'your-appsecret' 67: my_access_token = 'your-page-access-token' 68: FacebookAdsApi.init(my_app_id, my_app_secret, my_access_token) 69: my_account = AdAccount('act_') 70: campaigns = my_account.get_campaigns() 71: print(campaigns) 72: ``` 73: ### Test Your Install 74: Test your install with the following command: 75: ```python 76: python test.py 77: ``` 78: You should see the result in your terminal window. If it complains about an expired token, repeat the process for requesting a Page Access Token described in the prerequisites section above. 79: **NOTE**: We shall use the objects module throughout the rest of the tutorial. You can 80: also use the individual class files under adobjects directly. 81: ## Understanding CRUD 82: The SDK implements a CRUD (create, read, update, delete) design. Objects 83: relevant to exploring the graph are located in the objects module of the 84: facebook_business package. 85: All objects on the graph are instances of ``AbstractObject``. Some objects can 86: be directly queried and thus are instances of ``AbstractCrudObject`` (a subclass 87: of ``AbstractObject``). Both these abstract classes are located in 88: ``facebook_business.adobjects``. 89: There is and additional folder ``adobjects`` under facebook_business. Under this you will see a file for every ad object 90: in our Marketing API. These files are autogenerated from our API and therefore 91: are close in parity with what API has to offer. Based on what CRUD operations can be 92: performed on each object, you will see the presence of the following methods in them: 93: * ``api_get`` 94: * ``api_update`` 95: * ``api_delete`` 96: * ``create_xxx`` 97: * ``get_xxx`` 98: For example, Campaign has all these methods but AdAccount does not. Read the 99: Marketing API documentation for more information about 100: how different ad 101: objects are used. 102: There are some deprecated function in ``AbstractCrudObject``, like 103: * ``remote_create`` 104: * ``remote_read`` 105: * ``remote_update`` 106: * ``remote_delete`` 107: Please try to stop use them since we may plan to deprecated them soon. 108: ## Exploring the Graph 109: The way the SDK abstracts the API is by defining classes that represent objects 110: on the graph. These class definitions and their helpers are located in 111: ``facebook_business.adobjects``. 112: ### Initializing Objects 113: Look at ``AbstractObject``'s and ``AbstractCrudObject``'s ``__init__`` method 114: for more information. Most objects on the graph subclass from one of the two. 115: When instantiating an ad object, you can specify its id if it already exists by 116: defining ``fbid`` argument. Also, if you want to interact with the 117: API using a specific api object instead of the default, you can specify the 118: ``api`` argument. 119: ### Edges 120: Look at the methods of an object to see what associations over which we can 121: iterate. For example an ``User`` object has a method ``get_ad_accounts`` which 122: returns an iterator of ``AdAccount`` objects. 123: ### Ad Account 124: Most ad-related operations are in the context of an ad account. You can go to 125: Ads Manager to see accounts 126: for which you have permission. Most of you probably have a personal account. 127: Let's get all the ad accounts for the user with the given access token. I only 128: have one account so the following is printed: 129: ```python 130: >>> from facebook_business.adobjects.user import User 131: >>> me = adobjects.User(fbid='me') 132: >>> my_accounts = list(me.get_ad_accounts()) 133: >>> print(my_accounts) 134: [{ 'account_id': u'17842443', 'id': u'act_17842443'}] 135: >>> type(my_accounts[0]) 136: 137: ``` 138: **WARNING**: We do not specify a keyword argument ``api=api`` when instantiating 139: the ``User`` object here because we've already set the default api when 140: bootstrapping. 141: **NOTE**: We wrap the return value of ``get_ad_accounts`` with ``list()`` 142: because ``get_ad_accounts`` returns an ``EdgeIterator`` object (located in 143: ``facebook_business.adobjects``) and we want to get the full list right away instead of 144: having the iterator lazily loading accounts. 145: For our purposes, we can just pick an account and do our experiments in its 146: context: 147: ```python 148: >>> my_account = my_accounts[0] 149: ``` 150: Or if you already know your account id: 151: ```python 152: >>> my_account = adobjects.AdAccount('act_17842443') 153: ``` 154: ## Create 155: Let's create a campaign. It's in the context of the account, i.e. its parent 156: should be the account. 157: ```python 158: fields = [ 159: ] 160: params = { 161: adobjects.Campaign.Field.name : 'Conversions Campaign', 162: adobjects.Campaign.Field.configured_status: adobjects.Campaign.Status.paused, 163: } 164: campaign = AdAccount(id).create_campaign(fields, params) 165: ``` 166: Then we specify some details about the campaign. To figure out what properties 167: to define, you should look at the available fields of the object (located in 168: ``Campaign.Field``) and also look at the ad object's documentation (e.g. 169: 170: Campaign). 171: **NOTE**: To find out the fields, look at the individual class file under adobjects 172: directory. 173: If there's an error, an exception will be raised. Possible exceptions and their 174: descriptions are listed in ``facebook_business.exceptions``. 175: ## Read 176: We can also read properties of an object from the api assuming that the object 177: is already created and has a node path. Accessing properties of an object is 178: simple since ``AbstractObject`` implements the ``collections.MutableMapping``. 179: You can access them just like accessing a key of a dictionary: 180: ```python 181: >>> print(my_account) 182: {'account_id': u'17842443', 'id': u'act_17842443'} 183: >>> my_account = my_account.api_get(fields=[adobjects.AdAccount.Field.amount_spent]) 184: >>> print(my_account[adobjects.AdAccount.Field.amount_spent]) 185: {'amount_spent': 21167, 'account_id': u'17842443', 'id': u'act_17842443'} 186: ``` 187: ## Update 188: To update an object, we can modify its properties and then call the 189: ``api_update`` method to sync the object with the server. Let's correct the 190: typo "Campain" to "Campaign": 191: ```python 192: >>> campaign.api_update(fields=[], params={adobjects.Campaign.Field.name:"Potato Campaign"}) 193: ``` 194: You can see the results in ads manager. 195: ## Delete 196: If we decide we don't want the campaign we created anymore: 197: ```python 198: campaign.api_delete() 199: ``` 200: ## Useful Arguments 201: ### MULTIPLE ACCESS TOKENS 202: Throughout the docs, the method FacebookAdsApi.init is called before making any API calls. This 203: method set up a default FacebookAdsApi object to be used everywhere. That simplifies the usage 204: but it's not feasible when a system using the SDK will make calls on behalf of multiple users. 205: The reason why this is not feasible is because each user should have its own FacebookSession, with its own 206: access token, rather than using the same session for every one. Each session should be used to create a 207: separate FacebookAdsApi object. See example below: 208: ```python 209: my_app_id = '' 210: my_app_secret = '' 211: my_access_token_1 = '' 212: my_access_token_2 = '' 213: proxies = {'http': '', 'https': ''} # add proxies if needed 214: session1 = FacebookSession( 215: my_app_id, 216: my_app_secret, 217: my_access_token_1, 218: proxies, 219: ) 220: session2 = FacebookSession( 221: my_app_id, 222: my_app_secret, 223: my_access_token_2, 224: proxies, 225: ) 226: api1 = FacebookAdsApi(session1) 227: api2 = FacebookAdsApi(session2) 228: ``` 229: In the SDK examples, we always set a single FacebookAdsApi object as the default one. 230: However, working with multiples access_tokens, require us to use multiples apis. We may set a default 231: api for a user, but, for the other users, we shall use its the api object as a param. In the example below, 232: we create two AdUsers, the first one using the default api and the second one using its api object: 233: ```python 234: FacebookAdsApi.set_default_api(api1) 235: me1 = AdUser(fbid='me') 236: me2 = AdUser(fbid='me', api=api2) 237: ``` 238: Another way to create the same objects from above would be: 239: ```python 240: me1 = AdUser(fbid='me', api=api1) 241: me2 = AdUser(fbid='me', api=api2) 242: ``` 243: From here, all the following workflow for these objects remains the same. The only exceptions are 244: the classmethods calls, where we now should pass the api we want to use as the last parameter 245: on every call. For instance, a call to the Aduser.get_by_ids method should be like this: 246: ```python 247: session = FacebookSession( 248: my_app_id, 249: my_app_secret, 250: my_access_token_1, 251: proxies, 252: ) 253: api = FacebookAdsApi(session1) 254: Aduser.get_by_ids(ids=['', ''], api=api) 255: ``` 256: ### CRUD 257: All CRUD calls support a ``params`` keyword argument which takes a dictionary 258: mapping parameter names to values in case advanced modification is required. You 259: can find the list of parameter names as attributes of 260: ``{your object class}.Field``. Under the Field class there may be other classes 261: which contain, as attributes, valid fields of the value of one of the parent 262: properties. 263: ``api_update`` and ``create_xxx`` support a ``files`` keyword argument 264: which takes a dictionary mapping file reference names to binary opened file 265: objects. 266: ``api_get`` supports a ``fields`` keyword argument which is a convenient way 267: of specifying the 'fields' parameter. ``fields`` takes a list of fields which 268: should be read during the call. The valid fields can be found as attributes of 269: the class Field. 270: ### Edges 271: When initializing an ``EdgeIterator`` or when calling a method such as 272: ``AdAccount.get_ad_campaigns``: 273: * You can specify a ``fields`` argument which takes a list of fields to read for 274: the objects being read. 275: * You can specify a ``params`` argument that can help you specify or filter the 276: edge more precisely. 277: ## Batch Calling 278: It is efficient to group together large numbers of calls into one http request. 279: The SDK makes this process simple. You can group together calls into an instance 280: of ``FacebookAdsApiBatch`` (available in facebook_business.api). To easily get one 281: for your api instance: 282: ```python 283: my_api_batch = api.new_batch() 284: ``` 285: Calls can be added to the batch instead of being executed immediately: 286: ```python 287: campaign.api_delete(batch=my_api_batch) 288: ``` 289: Once you're finished adding calls to the batch, you can send off the request: 290: ```python 291: my_api_batch.execute() 292: ``` 293: Please follow 294: batch call guidelines in the Marketing API documentation. There are optimal 295: numbers of calls per batch. In addition, you may need to watch out that for rate 296: limiting as a batch call simply improves network performance and each call does 297: count individually towards rate limiting. 298: ## Exceptions 299: See ``facebook_business.exceptions`` for a list of exceptions which may be thrown by 300: the SDK. 301: ## Conversions API 302: The Business SDK includes a server-side client for the [Conversions API](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/conversions-api), used to send web, app, and offline events to Meta directly from your server. 303: ```python 304: import time 305: from facebook_business.adobjects.serverside.action_source import ActionSource 306: from facebook_business.adobjects.serverside.custom_data import CustomData 307: from facebook_business.adobjects.serverside.event import Event 308: from facebook_business.adobjects.serverside.event_request import EventRequest 309: from facebook_business.adobjects.serverside.user_data import UserData 310: from facebook_business.api import FacebookAdsApi 311: FacebookAdsApi.init(access_token='') 312: user_data = UserData( 313: email='joe@eg.com', 314: client_ip_address=request.META.get('REMOTE_ADDR'), 315: client_user_agent=request.headers['User-Agent'], 316: ) 317: custom_data = CustomData(currency='usd', value=123.45) 318: event = Event( 319: event_name='Purchase', 320: event_time=int(time.time()), 321: user_data=user_data, 322: custom_data=custom_data, 323: event_source_url='http://jaspers-market.com/product/123', 324: action_source=ActionSource.WEBSITE, 325: ) 326: response = EventRequest(pixel_id='', events=[event]).execute() 327: print(response) 328: ``` 329: For advanced features — asynchronous requests, concurrent batching, and a custom HTTP service — see [Meta Business SDK Features for Conversions API](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/conversions-api/guides/business-sdk-features/). 330: ### Conversions API Parameter Builder integration 331: The SDK bundles the [Conversions API Parameter Builder](https://github.com/facebook/capi-param-builder) ([Python README](https://github.com/facebook/capi-param-builder/blob/main/python/README.md)) so it can auto-fill key event parameters straight from the incoming HTTP request. Call `set_request_context()` on an event and pass the incoming request — see [Framework support](https://github.com/facebook/capi-param-builder/blob/main/python/README.md#framework-support) for exactly what to pass for your framework (e.g. a WSGI request such as Django `request` / Flask `request`, an ASGI scope, or a raw environ dict). At send time the SDK runs the Parameter Builder and fills in any of these fields you left empty: 332: - `user_data.fbc`, `user_data.fbp` 333: - `event_source_url`, `referrer_url` 334: ```python 335: from facebook_business.adobjects.serverside.preference import Preference 336: event = Event( 337: event_name='Purchase', 338: event_time=int(time.time()), 339: user_data=UserData(email='joe@eg.com'), 340: action_source=ActionSource.WEBSITE, 341: ).set_request_context(request) 342: # Optional: gate which fields may be auto-filled (all default True). 343: # Order: fbc, fbp, client_ip_address, referrer_url, event_source_url. 344: # .set_request_context(request, Preference(True, True, True, True, False)) 345: ``` 346: Auto-fill is **gated** by the optional `Preference` allowlist, **non-destructive** (a value you set yourself is never overwritten), and **order-independent**. Note that in Python, `client_ip_address` is not auto-derived yet — keep setting it (and `client_user_agent`) yourself. 347: ## Tests 348: ### Unit tests 349: The unit tests don't require an access token or network access. Run them 350: with your default installed Python as follows: 351: ``` 352: python -m facebook_business.test.unit 353: ``` 354: You can also use tox to run the unit tests with multiple Python versions: 355: ``` 356: sudo apt-get install python-tox # Debian/Ubuntu 357: sudo yum install python-tox # Fedora 358: tox --skip-missing-interpreters 359: ``` 360: You can increase interpreter coverage by installing additional versions of 361: Python. On Ubuntu you can use the 362: [deadsnakes PPA](https://launchpad.net/~fkrull/+archive/ubuntu/deadsnakes). 363: On other distributions you can 364: [build from source](https://www.python.org/downloads/) and then use 365: `sudo make altinstall` to avoid conflicts with your system-installed 366: version. 367: ## Examples 368: Examples of usage are located in the ``examples/`` folder. 369: ## Debug 370: If this SDK is not working as expected, it may be either a SDK issue or API issue. 371: This can be identified by constructing a raw cURL request and seeing if the response is as expected 372: for example: 373: ```python 374: from facebook_business.adobjects.page import Page 375: from facebook_business.api import FacebookAdsApi 376: FacebookAdsApi.init(access_token=access_token, debug=True) 377: page = Page(page_id).api_get(fields=fields,params=params) 378: ``` 379: When running this code, this cURL request will be printed to the console as: 380: ``` 381: curl -X 'GET' -H 'Accept: */*' -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate' -H 'Connection: keep-alive' -H 'User-Agent: fbbizsdk-python-v3.3.1' 'https://graph.facebook.com/v3.3//?access_token=&fields=name%2Cbirthday%2Cphone' 382: ``` 383: ## SDK Codegen 384: Our SDK is autogenerated from [SDK Codegen](https://github.com/facebook/facebook-business-sdk-codegen). If you want to learn more about how our SDK code is generated, please check this repository. 385: ## Issue 386: Since we want to handle bugs more efficiently, we've decided to close issue reporting in Github and move to our dedicated bug reporting channel. 387: If you encounter a bug with Business SDK (Python), please report the issue at [our developer bug reporting channel](https://developers.facebook.com/support/bugs/). 388: ## License 389: Facebook Business SDK for Python is licensed under the LICENSE file in the root directory of this source tree.

1: # Meta Ads MCP
2: A [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server that lets AI assistants — Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Cursor, or any MCP client — run your Meta Ads end to end: launch campaigns, upload creatives, update budgets, and analyze performance through natural conversation across Facebook, Instagram, and every Meta ad surface. Available as a **hosted remote MCP** — no developer token, no self-hosting required.
3: This is the **Meta Ads node** of the [Pipeboard](https://pipeboard.co) MCP family — five remote MCP servers (Meta, Google, TikTok, Snap, Reddit) plus a unified [Pipeboard CLI](https://github.com/pipeboard-co/pipeboard-cli), **230+ tools** in total, one auth, one safety model. If you are comparing single-platform MCPs, you are looking at one node of a network — see [The Pipeboard MCP Family](#the-pipeboard-mcp-family) below.
4: > **Note:** This is an independent open-source project that uses Meta's public APIs. The hosted service behind it — [Pipeboard](https://pipeboard.co) — is a **badged Meta Business Partner** and an officially approved Meta app that manages **Meta, Google, TikTok, Snap & Reddit Ads** from one login (with a free plan) — so it is neither Meta-only nor something you have to self-host. Meta, Facebook, Instagram, and other Meta brand names are trademarks of their respective owners.
5: [![Meta Ads MCP Server Demo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e605cee-d289-414b-814c-6299e7f3383e)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e605cee-d289-414b-814c-6299e7f3383e)
6: [![MCP Badge](https://lobehub.com/badge/mcp/nictuku-meta-ads-mcp)](https://lobehub.com/mcp/nictuku-meta-ads-mcp)
7: mcp-name: co.pipeboard/meta-ads-mcp
8: ## Community & Support

10: - [Email Support](mailto:info@pipeboard.co). Email us for support.
11: ## Table of Contents

23: ## The Pipeboard MCP Family
24: Pipeboard ships a remote [MCP server](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) for every major ad platform — plus a single-binary [CLI](https://github.com/pipeboard-co/pipeboard-cli) that wraps all of them. **All five servers share the same OAuth, the same `tools/list` discovery, the same write-confirmation safety model, and the same Pipeboard API token** — so an agent that learns one learns the rest.
25: ### Remote MCP servers
26: | Platform | Remote MCP URL | Surface |
27: |---|---|---|
28: | **Meta Ads MCP** (Facebook + Instagram) | `https://meta-ads.mcp.pipeboard.co/` | **42 tools** — campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives (incl. dynamic creative testing), image upload, insights, interest / behavior / demographic / geo targeting, page management |
29: | **Google Ads MCP** | `https://google-ads.mcp.pipeboard.co/` | **59 tools** — campaigns, ad groups, responsive search ads, Performance Max, keywords, GAQL queries, extensions (sitelinks, callouts, structured snippets), audiences, asset uploads, generic mutate |
30: | **TikTok Ads MCP** | `https://tiktok-ads.mcp.pipeboard.co/` | **59 tools** — campaigns, ad groups, ads, identities, image and video upload, audience and creative management, insights |
31: | **Snap Ads MCP** | `https://snap-ads.mcp.pipeboard.co/` | **37 tools** — ad accounts, campaigns, ad squads, ads, creatives, media upload, insights |
32: | **Reddit Ads MCP** | `https://reddit-ads.mcp.pipeboard.co/` | **33 tools** — accounts, campaigns, ad groups, ads, performance reports |
33: **That is 230+ tools across five ad platforms behind one auth.** Plug any of these URLs into Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, Perplexity, or any MCP-compatible client. Connect your ad accounts once at [pipeboard.co](https://pipeboard.co) and every client gets access.
34: ### Pipeboard CLI — the same tools, in your shell
35: [**Pipeboard CLI**](https://github.com/pipeboard-co/pipeboard-cli) is a single Go binary that exposes every MCP tool above as a typed shell command — built for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cline, OpenClaw, Codex) and automation scripts that prefer subprocess calls over JSON-RPC:
36: ```bash
37: brew install pipeboard-co/tap/pipeboard
38: export PIPEBOARD_API_TOKEN=<your-token>
39: pipeboard meta-ads get-campaigns --account-id act_123
40: pipeboard google-ads execute-gaql-query --customer-id 1234567890 --query "..."
41: pipeboard tiktok-ads get-campaigns --advertiser-id 7605685552884596737
42: ```
43: Sub-50ms startup, no MCP handshake per call, all five platforms in one binary. Full docs in the [pipeboard-cli repo](https://github.com/pipeboard-co/pipeboard-cli).
44: ### Why a family instead of one MCP per repo?
45: - **One account, every platform** — auth once at [pipeboard.co](https://pipeboard.co); manage Meta + Google + TikTok + Snap + Reddit from the same agent session
46: - **Cross-platform questions get cross-platform answers** — "which channel had the cheapest signups last week?" actually works
47: - **Same safety contract everywhere** — writes are explicit, new campaigns start paused where the platform supports it, and confirmation prompts look identical across all five servers
48: - **One token, one rate-limit ceiling, one place to revoke** — no juggling separate OAuth flows or per-vendor installs
49: Single-platform MCP benchmarks miss the point. The value is the network, not the node.
50: ### How Pipeboard compares
51: If you are choosing between the ways to run Meta Ads from an AI assistant, here is the honest landscape:
52: | | **Pipeboard** | **Meta's official MCP** | **Open-source / self-hosted servers** |
53: |---|---|---|---|
54: | **Platforms** | Meta + Google + TikTok + Snap + Reddit, one login | Meta only | Usually Meta only |
55: | **Setup** | Hosted remote MCP — no developer token, ~2 minutes | Hosted by Meta (Meta only) | Self-host, manage your own tokens & upgrades |
56: | **Trust** | Badged Meta Business Partner + approved Meta app | First-party (Meta) | Varies — audit the code yourself |
57: | **Safety** | Explicit confirmation on every write; new campaigns start paused | Meta-defined | You build the guardrails |
58: | **Price** | Free plan, then paid tiers | Free (open beta) | Free, but you run the infra |
59: Meta's official connector is the safest **single-platform** option. Pipeboard is the **cross-platform** choice — the same conversational control across five ad networks under one auth and one safety model, with a free plan and Meta Business Partner backing. Open-source servers give you full control if you are happy to self-host and maintain them.
60: ## Getting started with Remote MCP (Recommended)
61: The fastest and most reliable way to get started is to **[🚀 Get started with our Meta Ads Remote MCP](https://pipeboard.co)**. Our cloud service uses streamable HTTP transport for reliable, scalable access to your Meta Ads account. No technical setup required — just connect and start launching, updating, and analyzing campaigns with AI!
62: ### For Claude Pro/Max Users
63: 1. Go to [claude.ai/settings/integrations](https://claude.ai/settings/integrations) (requires Claude Pro or Max)
64: 2. Click "Add Integration" and enter:
65: - **Name**: "Pipeboard Meta Ads" (or any name you prefer)
66: - **Integration URL**: `https://meta-ads.mcp.pipeboard.co/`
67: 3. Click "Connect" next to the integration and follow the prompts to:
68: - Login to Pipeboard
69: - Connect your Facebook Ads account
70: That's it! You can now ask Claude to analyze your Meta ad campaigns, get performance insights, and manage your advertising.
71: #### Advanced: Direct Token Authentication (Claude)
72: For direct token-based authentication without the interactive flow, use this URL format when adding the integration:
73: ```
74: https://meta-ads.mcp.pipeboard.co/?token=YOUR_PIPEBOARD_TOKEN
75: ```
76: Get your token at [pipeboard.co/api-tokens](https://pipeboard.co/api-tokens).
77: ### For Cursor Users
78: Add the following to your `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Once you enable the remote MCP, click on "Needs login" to finish the login process.
79: ```json
80: {
81: "mcpServers": {
82: "meta-ads-remote": {
83: "url": "https://meta-ads.mcp.pipeboard.co/"
84: }
85: }
86: }
87: ```
88: #### Advanced: Direct Token Authentication (Cursor)
89: If you prefer to authenticate without the interactive login flow, you can include your Pipeboard API token directly in the URL:
90: ```json
91: {
92: "mcpServers": {
93: "meta-ads-remote": {
94: "url": "https://meta-ads.mcp.pipeboard.co/?token=YOUR_PIPEBOARD_TOKEN"
95: }
96: }
97: }
98: ```
99: Get your token at [pipeboard.co/api-tokens](https://pipeboard.co/api-tokens).
100: ### For Other MCP Clients
101: Use the Remote MCP URL: `https://meta-ads.mcp.pipeboard.co/`
102: **[📖 Get detailed setup instructions for your AI client here](https://pipeboard.co)**
103: #### Advanced: Direct Token Authentication (OpenClaw and other clients)
104: For MCP clients that support token-based authentication, you can append your Pipeboard API token to the URL:
105: ```
106: https://meta-ads.mcp.pipeboard.co/?token=YOUR_PIPEBOARD_TOKEN
107: ```
108: This bypasses the interactive login flow and authenticates immediately. Get your token at [pipeboard.co/api-tokens](https://pipeboard.co/api-tokens).
109: ### Other platforms
110: Meta Ads is one of five remote MCP servers in the family — see [The Pipeboard MCP Family](#the-pipeboard-mcp-family) for Google Ads, TikTok Ads, Snap Ads, and Reddit Ads, all set up the same way.
111: ## Pipeboard CLI (Alternative to MCP)
112: If your agent prefers shell commands over JSON-RPC, the [Pipeboard CLI](https://github.com/pipeboard-co/pipeboard-cli) exposes every tool in the family as a typed subcommand — see [the family section above](#pipeboard-cli--the-same-tools-in-your-shell) for the quick install and the [pipeboard-cli repo](https://github.com/pipeboard-co/pipeboard-cli) for full docs.
113: ## Local Installation (Advanced Technical Users Only)
114: 🚀 **We strongly recommend using [Remote MCP](https://pipeboard.co) instead** - it's faster, more reliable, and requires no technical setup.
115: Meta Ads MCP also supports a local streamable HTTP transport, allowing you to run it as a standalone HTTP API for web applications and custom integrations. See **[Streamable HTTP Setup Guide](STREAMABLE_HTTP_SETUP.md)** for complete instructions.
116: ## Features
117: - **Campaign Management**: Launch campaigns, ad sets, and ads, update budgets, pause and resume, and apply targeting changes — all from a conversation, with explicit confirmation on every write
118: - **Creative Operations**: Upload images, build creatives, and update copy, headlines, descriptions, and CTAs without leaving your AI client
119: - **Dynamic Creative Testing**: One API for both simple ads (single headline/description) and full A/B testing (multiple headlines/descriptions)
120: - **AI-Powered Campaign Analysis**: Let your favorite LLM analyze performance and surface actionable insights
121: - **Strategic Recommendations**: Receive data-backed suggestions for optimizing ad spend, targeting, and creative content
122: - **Budget Optimization**: Get recommendations for reallocating budget to better-performing ad sets
123: - **Creative Improvement**: Receive feedback on ad copy, imagery, and calls-to-action
124: - **Automated Monitoring**: Ask any MCP-compatible LLM to track performance metrics and alert you about significant changes
125: - **Cross-Platform Integration**: Works with Facebook, Instagram, and all Meta ad surfaces
126: - **Universal LLM Support**: Compatible with any MCP client including Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cherry Studio, and more
127: - **Partner-Backed, Not Just Open Source**: Built by [Pipeboard](https://pipeboard.co), a badged Meta Business Partner and officially approved Meta app — with a free plan and hosted remote MCP (no self-hosting required)
128: - **Enhanced Search**: Generic search function includes page searching when queries mention "page" or "pages"
129: - **Simple Authentication**: Easy setup with secure OAuth authentication
130: - **Cross-Platform Support**: Works on Windows, macOS, and Linux
131: ## Configuration
132: ### Remote MCP (Recommended)
133: **[✨ Get started with Remote MCP here](https://pipeboard.co)** - no technical setup required! Just connect your Facebook Ads account and start asking AI to analyze your campaigns.
134: ### Local Installation (Advanced Technical Users)
135: For advanced users who need to self-host, the package can be installed from source. Local installations require creating your own Meta Developer App. **We recommend using [Remote MCP](https://pipeboard.co) for a simpler experience.**
136: ### Available MCP Tools
137: 1. `mcp_meta_ads_get_ad_accounts`
138: - Get ad accounts accessible by a user
139: - Inputs:
140: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
141: - `user_id`: Meta user ID or "me" for the current user
142: - `limit`: Maximum number of accounts to return (default: 200)
143: - Returns: List of accessible ad accounts with their details
144: 2. `mcp_meta_ads_get_account_info`
145: - Get detailed information about a specific ad account
146: - Inputs:
147: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
148: - `account_id`: Meta Ads account ID (format: act_XXXXXXXXX)
149: - Returns: Detailed information about the specified account
150: 3. `mcp_meta_ads_get_account_pages`
151: - Get pages associated with a Meta Ads account
152: - Inputs:
153: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
154: - `account_id`: Meta Ads account ID (format: act_XXXXXXXXX) or "me" for the current user's pages
155: - Returns: List of pages associated with the account, useful for ad creation and management
156: 4. `mcp_meta_ads_get_campaigns`
157: - Get campaigns for a Meta Ads account with optional filtering
158: - Inputs:
159: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
160: - `account_id`: Meta Ads account ID (format: act_XXXXXXXXX)
161: - `limit`: Maximum number of campaigns to return (default: 10)
162: - `status_filter`: Filter by status (empty for all, or 'ACTIVE', 'PAUSED', etc.)
163: - Returns: List of campaigns matching the criteria
164: 5. `mcp_meta_ads_get_campaign_details`
165: - Get detailed information about a specific campaign
166: - Inputs:
167: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
168: - `campaign_id`: Meta Ads campaign ID
169: - Returns: Detailed information about the specified campaign
170: 6. `mcp_meta_ads_create_campaign`
171: - Create a new campaign in a Meta Ads account
172: - Inputs:
173: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
174: - `account_id`: Meta Ads account ID (format: act_XXXXXXXXX)
175: - `name`: Campaign name
176: - `objective`: Campaign objective (ODAX, outcome-based). Must be one of:
177: - `OUTCOME_AWARENESS`
178: - `OUTCOME_TRAFFIC`
179: - `OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT`
180: - `OUTCOME_LEADS`
181: - `OUTCOME_SALES`
182: - `OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION`
183: Note: Legacy objectives such as `BRAND_AWARENESS`, `LINK_CLICKS`, `CONVERSIONS`, `APP_INSTALLS`, etc. are no longer valid for new campaigns and will cause a 400 error. Use the outcome-based values above. Common mappings:
184: - `BRAND_AWARENESS` → `OUTCOME_AWARENESS`
185: - `REACH` → `OUTCOME_AWARENESS`
186: - `LINK_CLICKS`, `TRAFFIC` → `OUTCOME_TRAFFIC`
187: - `POST_ENGAGEMENT`, `PAGE_LIKES`, `EVENT_RESPONSES`, `VIDEO_VIEWS` → `OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT`
188: - `LEAD_GENERATION` → `OUTCOME_LEADS`
189: - `CONVERSIONS`, `CATALOG_SALES`, `MESSAGES` (sales-focused flows) → `OUTCOME_SALES`
190: - `APP_INSTALLS` → `OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION`
191: - `status`: Initial campaign status (default: PAUSED)
192: - `special_ad_categories`: List of special ad categories if applicable
193: - `daily_budget`: Daily budget in account currency (in cents)
194: - `lifetime_budget`: Lifetime budget in account currency (in cents)
195: - `bid_strategy`: Bid strategy. Must be one of: `LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP`, `LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP`, `COST_CAP`, `LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS`.
196: - Returns: Confirmation with new campaign details
197: - Example:
198: ```json
199: {
200: "name": "2025 - Bedroom Furniture - Awareness",
201: "account_id": "act_123456789012345",
202: "objective": "OUTCOME_AWARENESS",
203: "special_ad_categories": [],
204: "status": "PAUSED",
205: "buying_type": "AUCTION",
206: "bid_strategy": "LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP",
207: "daily_budget": 10000
208: }
209: ```
210: 7. `mcp_meta_ads_get_adsets`
211: - Get ad sets for a Meta Ads account with optional filtering by campaign
212: - Inputs:
213: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
214: - `account_id`: Meta Ads account ID (format: act_XXXXXXXXX)
215: - `limit`: Maximum number of ad sets to return (default: 10)
216: - `campaign_id`: Optional campaign ID to filter by
217: - Returns: List of ad sets matching the criteria
218: 8. `mcp_meta_ads_get_adset_details`
219: - Get detailed information about a specific ad set
220: - Inputs:
221: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
222: - `adset_id`: Meta Ads ad set ID
223: - Returns: Detailed information about the specified ad set
224: 9. `mcp_meta_ads_create_adset`
225: - Create a new ad set in a Meta Ads account
226: - Inputs:
227: - `account_id`: Meta Ads account ID (format: act_XXXXXXXXX)
228: - `campaign_id`: Meta Ads campaign ID this ad set belongs to
229: - `name`: Ad set name
230: - `status`: Initial ad set status (default: PAUSED)
231: - `daily_budget`: Daily budget in account currency (in cents) as a string
232: - `lifetime_budget`: Lifetime budget in account currency (in cents) as a string
233: - `targeting`: Targeting specifications (e.g., age, location, interests)
234: - `optimization_goal`: Conversion optimization goal (e.g., 'LINK_CLICKS')
235: - `billing_event`: How you're charged (e.g., 'IMPRESSIONS')
236: - `bid_amount`: Bid amount in cents. Required for LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP, COST_CAP, TARGET_COST.
237: - `bid_strategy`: Bid strategy (e.g., 'LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP', 'LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS')
238: - `bid_constraints`: Bid constraints dict. Required for LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS (e.g., `{"roas_average_floor": 20000}`)
239: - `start_time`, `end_time`: Optional start/end times (ISO 8601)
240: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token
241: - Returns: Confirmation with new ad set details
242: 10. `mcp_meta_ads_get_ads`
243: - Get ads for a Meta Ads account with optional filtering
244: - Inputs:
245: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
246: - `account_id`: Meta Ads account ID (format: act_XXXXXXXXX)
247: - `limit`: Maximum number of ads to return (default: 10)
248: - `campaign_id`: Optional campaign ID to filter by
249: - `adset_id`: Optional ad set ID to filter by
250: - Returns: List of ads matching the criteria
251: 11. `mcp_meta_ads_create_ad`
252: - Create a new ad with an existing creative
253: - Inputs:
254: - `account_id`: Meta Ads account ID (format: act_XXXXXXXXX)
255: - `name`: Ad name
256: - `adset_id`: Ad set ID where this ad will be placed
257: - `creative_id`: ID of an existing creative to use
258: - `status`: Initial ad status (default: PAUSED)
259: - `bid_amount`: Optional bid amount (in cents)
260: - `tracking_specs`: Optional tracking specifications
261: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token
262: - Returns: Confirmation with new ad details
263: 12. `mcp_meta_ads_get_ad_details`
264: - Get detailed information about a specific ad
265: - Inputs:
266: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
267: - `ad_id`: Meta Ads ad ID
268: - Returns: Detailed information about the specified ad
269: 13. `mcp_meta_ads_get_ad_creatives`
270: - Get creative details for a specific ad
271: - Inputs:
272: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
273: - `ad_id`: Meta Ads ad ID
274: - Returns: Creative details including text, images, and URLs
275: 14. `mcp_meta_ads_create_ad_creative`
276: - Create a new ad creative using an uploaded image hash
277: - Inputs:
278: - `account_id`: Meta Ads account ID (format: act_XXXXXXXXX)
279: - `name`: Creative name
280: - `image_hash`: Hash of the uploaded image
281: - `page_id`: Facebook Page ID for the ad
282: - `link_url`: Destination URL
283: - `message`: Ad copy/text
284: - `headline`: Single headline for simple ads (cannot be used with headlines)
285: - `headlines`: List of headlines for dynamic creative testing (cannot be used with headline)
286: - `description`: Single description for simple ads (cannot be used with descriptions)
287: - `descriptions`: List of descriptions for dynamic creative testing (cannot be used with description)
288: - `dynamic_creative_spec`: Dynamic creative optimization settings
289: - `call_to_action_type`: CTA button type (e.g., 'LEARN_MORE')
290: - `instagram_actor_id`: Optional Instagram account ID
291: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token
292: - Returns: Confirmation with new creative details
293: 15. `mcp_meta_ads_update_ad_creative`
294: - Update an existing ad creative with new content or settings
295: - Inputs:
296: - `creative_id`: Meta Ads creative ID to update
297: - `name`: New creative name
298: - `message`: New ad copy/text
299: - `headline`: Single headline for simple ads (cannot be used with headlines)
300: - `headlines`: New list of headlines for dynamic creative testing (cannot be used with headline)
301: - `description`: Single description for simple ads (cannot be used with descriptions)
302: - `descriptions`: New list of descriptions for dynamic creative testing (cannot be used with description)
303: - `dynamic_creative_spec`: New dynamic creative optimization settings
304: - `call_to_action_type`: New call to action button type
305: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
306: - Returns: Confirmation with updated creative details
307: 16. `mcp_meta_ads_upload_ad_image`
308: - Upload an image to use in Meta Ads creatives
309: - Inputs:
310: - `account_id`: Meta Ads account ID (format: act_XXXXXXXXX)
311: - `image_path`: Path to the image file to upload
312: - `name`: Optional name for the image
313: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token
314: - Returns: JSON response with image details including hash
315: 17. `mcp_meta_ads_get_ad_image`
316: - Get, download, and visualize a Meta ad image in one step
317: - Inputs:
318: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
319: - `ad_id`: Meta Ads ad ID
320: - Returns: The ad image ready for direct visual analysis
321: 18. `mcp_meta_ads_update_ad`
322: - Update an ad with new settings
323: - Inputs:
324: - `ad_id`: Meta Ads ad ID
325: - `status`: Update ad status (ACTIVE, PAUSED, etc.)
326: - `bid_amount`: Bid amount in account currency (in cents for USD)
327: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
328: - Returns: Confirmation with updated ad details and a confirmation link
329: 19. `mcp_meta_ads_update_adset`
330: - Update an ad set with new settings including frequency caps
331: - Inputs:
332: - `adset_id`: Meta Ads ad set ID
333: - `frequency_control_specs`: List of frequency control specifications
334: - `bid_strategy`: Bid strategy (e.g., 'LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP', 'LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS')
335: - `bid_amount`: Bid amount in cents. Required for LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP, COST_CAP, TARGET_COST.
336: - `bid_constraints`: Bid constraints dict. Required for LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS (e.g., `{"roas_average_floor": 20000}`)
337: - `status`: Update ad set status (ACTIVE, PAUSED, etc.)
338: - `targeting`: Targeting specifications including targeting_automation
339: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
340: - Returns: Confirmation with updated ad set details and a confirmation link
341: 20. `mcp_meta_ads_get_insights`
342: - Get performance insights for a campaign, ad set, ad or account
343: - Inputs:
344: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
345: - `object_id`: ID of the campaign, ad set, ad or account
346: - `time_range`: Time range for insights (default: maximum)
347: - `breakdown`: Optional breakdown dimension (e.g., age, gender, country)
348: - `level`: Level of aggregation (ad, adset, campaign, account)
349: - `action_attribution_windows` (optional): List of attribution windows for conversion data (e.g., ["1d_click", "1d_view", "7d_click", "7d_view"]). When specified, actions and cost_per_action_type include additional fields for each window. The 'value' field always shows 7d_click attribution.
350: - Returns: Performance metrics for the specified object
351: 21. `mcp_meta_ads_get_login_link`
352: - Get a clickable login link for Meta Ads authentication
353: - Inputs:
354: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
355: - Returns: A clickable resource link for Meta authentication
356: 22. `mcp_meta_ads_create_budget_schedule`
357: - Create a budget schedule for a Meta Ads campaign
358: - Inputs:
359: - `campaign_id`: Meta Ads campaign ID
360: - `budget_value`: Amount of budget increase
361: - `budget_value_type`: Type of budget value ("ABSOLUTE" or "MULTIPLIER")
362: - `time_start`: Unix timestamp for when the high demand period should start
363: - `time_end`: Unix timestamp for when the high demand period should end
364: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token
365: - Returns: JSON string with the ID of the created budget schedule or an error message
366: 23. `mcp_meta_ads_search_interests`
367: - Search for interest targeting options by keyword
368: - Inputs:
369: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
370: - `query`: Search term for interests (e.g., "baseball", "cooking", "travel")
371: - `limit`: Maximum number of results to return (default: 25)
372: - Returns: Interest data with id, name, audience_size, and path fields
373: 24. `mcp_meta_ads_get_interest_suggestions`
374: - Get interest suggestions based on existing interests
375: - Inputs:
376: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
377: - `interest_list`: List of interest names to get suggestions for (e.g., ["Basketball", "Soccer"])
378: - `limit`: Maximum number of suggestions to return (default: 25)
379: - Returns: Suggested interests with id, name, audience_size, and description fields
380: 25. `mcp_meta_ads_validate_interests`
381: - Validate interest names or IDs for targeting
382: - Inputs:
383: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
384: - `interest_list`: List of interest names to validate (e.g., ["Japan", "Basketball"])
385: - `interest_fbid_list`: List of interest IDs to validate (e.g., ["6003700426513"])
386: - Returns: Validation results showing valid status and audience_size for each interest
387: 26. `mcp_meta_ads_search_behaviors`
388: - Get all available behavior targeting options
389: - Inputs:
390: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
391: - `limit`: Maximum number of results to return (default: 50)
392: - Returns: Behavior targeting options with id, name, audience_size bounds, path, and description
393: 27. `mcp_meta_ads_search_demographics`
394: - Get demographic targeting options
395: - Inputs:
396: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
397: - `demographic_class`: Type of demographics ('demographics', 'life_events', 'industries', 'income', 'family_statuses', 'user_device', 'user_os')
398: - `limit`: Maximum number of results to return (default: 50)
399: - Returns: Demographic targeting options with id, name, audience_size bounds, path, and description
400: 28. `mcp_meta_ads_search_geo_locations`
401: - Search for geographic targeting locations
402: - Inputs:
403: - `access_token` (optional): Meta API access token (will use cached token if not provided)
404: - `query`: Search term for locations (e.g., "New York", "California", "Japan")
405: - `location_types`: Types of locations to search (['country', 'region', 'city', 'zip', 'geo_market', 'electoral_district'])
406: - `limit`: Maximum number of results to return (default: 25)
407: - Returns: Location data with key, name, type, and geographic hierarchy information

31: What is a Company Page/Organization?
32: A Company Page is an entity that represents an organization on LinkedIn. The Company Page is where a company can post organic content and interact with members on LinkedIn. In addition to the Ad Account, the Company Page is one of the key entities that's used across marketing APIs for both sponsored and organic use cases.
33: See Creating a LinkedIn Page guide for instructions on creating a company page.
34: Note
35: Company Pages are also referred to as "Organizations", and these terms are used interchangeably in the documentation.
36: Company Page Roles
37: Company Pages can be managed by members who have been granted one of the following roles within that Company Page.
38: Role
39: Description
40: ADMINISTRATOR
41: Administer an organizational entity; Post updates; Edit the organization page; Manage administrators; View analytics and notifications
42: DIRECT_SPONSORED_CONTENT_POSTER
43: Create/View direct sponsored content (DSC) for an organizational entity
44: RECRUITING_POSTER
45: Post to an organizational entity
46: LEAD_CAPTURE_ADMINISTRATOR
47: View/Manage landing pages for the company; Create/Edit landing pages
48: LEAD_GEN_FORMS_MANAGER
49: Access leads that belong to a specific account which is associated with a company page
50: ANALYST
51: Access to view an organization's private administrative data that relates to its social presence on LinkedIn, access limited to analytics tab to monitor the Page’s performance to help drive goals. Can edit the competitors of a page.
52: CURATOR
53: Access to broadcast content to employees of the organization, view Content Suggestions, create recommended content, and view and export Page analytics. Can edit the competitors of a page.
54: CONTENT_ADMINISTRATOR
55: Access to create and manage Page content, including updates, pinned posts, boosting updates, events, jobs etc.
56: The creator of the Company Page is the Administrator by default. All others can be added and given roles through the UI. Click "Admin tools" on the right side of the admin view of the Company Page and then select "Manage Admins". To add a member to a company page you must be connected on LinkedIn.
57: What is an Ad Account?
58: An Ad Account (a.k.a. Sponsored Account) is an umbrella entity for advertising management on LinkedIn, e.g., billing, campaigns, ad creatives, tracking tags, and more.
59: Ad Accounts can be managed through the UI using the Campaign Manager tool. Learn how to access Campaign Manager from the LinkedIn homepage, or for more information see Campaign Manager Overview
60: Ad Account Roles
61: Ad Accounts can be managed by members who have been granted one of the following roles within that Ad Account. Please note that you must be connected to a LinkedIn member to add them to a Company Page.
62: Role
63: Description
64: VIEWER
65: View campaign data and reports (can't Create/Edit campaigns or ads)
66: CREATIVE_MANAGER
67: Create/Edit/View campaign data and reports; Create/Edit ads
68: CAMPAIGN_MANAGER
69: View campaign data and reports; Create/Edit campaigns and ads
70: ACCOUNT_MANAGER
71: View campaign data and reports. Create/Edit campaigns and ads; Edit account data and manage user access
72: ACCOUNT_BILLING_ADMIN
73: View campaign data and reports; Create/Edit campaigns and ads. Edit account data and manage user access. Can also access billing data and will be billed for this account. (See next paragraph for more details on this role
74: Account Billing Admin role
75: There should be only one ACCOUNT_BILLING_ADMIN user role for an account.
76: The creator of the Ad Account is assigned Account Billing Administrator by default.
77: Other roles can be added and given roles through the UI.
78: Click the gear icon in the upper right corner of Campaign Manager and then select "Manage Access".
79: Managing Your Ad Accounts List
80: Once your application has been accepted into the Development Tier, you can manage and view your Ad Accounts from the developer portal. Add up to 5 accounts to manage in the Development Tier.
81: Select your application from the list of apps..
82: Click the "Products" tab in the navigation.
83: Click the "View settings" link next to "Advertising API".
84: Add or remove Ad Accounts from this page .
85: Only accounts that have been configured for access in the Ad Accounts tab of your application can be managed through the API.
86: You can't create new accounts through the API in the Development Tier.
87: How do Company Pages and Ad Accounts relate to each other?
88: Company Pages can be associated with Ad Accounts to advertise on behalf of that organization. For example, if an organization wanted to boost exposure to their Company Page's content by sponsoring it, they would need to associate their Company Page with an Ad Account.
89: While not required, we recommended that you always associate a Company Page with an Ad Account to get the full benefits of LinkedIn's marketing capabilities. Some campaign objectives and ad creative types require a Company Page to be associated with the Ad Account.
90: A Company Page can be associated with multiple Ad Accounts.
91: An Ad Account can only be associated with a single Company Page.
92: Once an Ad Account is linked to a particular Company Page, it can't be changed.
93: How do I make API calls on behalf of a LinkedIn member?
94: Once you have a developer application that has been given access to the LinkedIn Marketing API Program, you're ready to start generating OAuth access tokens to make API calls on behalf of authenticated members.
95: Before an API call can be made, any required permission scopes must first be granted by the LinkedIn member. This ensures that members are made aware of what an application could potentially access or do on their behalf.
96: If your application requires multiple permissions to access all the data it requires, members who use your application are required to accept all of them. They can't accept only a subset of the requested application permissions. To provide the best experience for the member, ensure that your application requests the fewest necessary permissions.
97: How do I know what roles a member has?
98: One of the common errors developers encounter is attempting to make API calls to Company Pages, Ad Accounts, and their associated objects using a token belonging to a member who doesn't have a role defined under a given Company Page or Ad Account. Use the /adAccountUsers and /organizationAcls API to validate what roles a member has.
99: The LinkedIn Advertising API gives you access to the following permissions. All these permission scopes are 3-legged permissions requiring explicit consent from a LinkedIn member. The 2-legged client credentials flow is not available for any marketing use cases.
100: Permission
101: Description
102: rw_organization_admin
103: Manage an authenticated member’s company pages and retrieve reporting data.
104: r_organization_admin
105: Retrieve your organization's pages and their reporting data (including follower, visitor, and content analytics).
106: w_organization_social
107: Post, comment, and like posts on behalf of an organization. Restricted to organizations in which the authenticated member has one of the following company page roles:
108: ADMINISTRATOR
109: DIRECT_SPONSORED_CONTENT_POSTER
110: LEAD_GEN_FORMS_MANAGER
111: r_organization_social
112: Retrieve organizations' posts, comments, and likes.
113: w_member_social
114: Post, comment, and like posts on behalf of an authenticated member.
115: rw_ads
116: Manage and read an authenticated member's ad accounts. Restricted to ad accounts in which the authenticated member has one of the following ad account roles:
117: ACCOUNT_BILLING_ADMIN
118: ACCOUNT_MANAGER
119: CAMPAIGN_MANAGER
120: CREATIVE_MANAGER
121: r_ads
122: Read an authenticated member's Ad Accounts. Restricted to ad accounts in which the authenticated member has one of the following Ad Account roles:
123: ACCOUNT_BILLING_ADMIN
124: ACCOUNT_MANAGER
125: CAMPAIGN_MANAGER
126: CREATIVE_MANAGER
127: VIEWER
128: r_ads_reporting
129: Retrieve reporting for advertising accounts.
130: r_1st_connections_size
131: Retrieve the count of an authenticated member's 1st-degree connections.
132: r_basicprofile
133: Read an authenticated member's basic profile including name, photo, headline, and public profile URL.
134: In addition to these permissions, members must have the appropriate roles as defined in Company Page Roles and Ad Account Roles to act on or read data from a given Company Page or Ad Account. See How Do I Know What Roles a Member Has to determine which roles an authenticated member has through the API.
135: One of the common errors developers encounter is attempting to make API calls to Company Pages, Ad Accounts, and their associated objects using a token belonging to a member who doesn't have a role defined under a given Company Page or Ad Account. Use the API to validate what roles a member has.
